intro.tourSteps: Here's what I see on your page now, top to bottom.
intro.jobsBuilding: These are the jobs you gave me. I'm reading them with your goals to find your strengths and the paths that fit. Your new page comes right after this.
intro.jobsStopped: These are the jobs you gave me.
intro.answersBuilding: I'm reading your answers now. Your new page comes right after this.

demo.note: This is a demo with a sample page. Nothing is sent to t.ROY.

failure.countsToward: Each try counts toward today's builds.

limit.title: Today's limit is used up
limit.bodyToday: You've hit today's limit for building with t.ROY. You can try again after {time} today. Your answers stay in this browser until then, unless you clear this computer.
limit.bodyTomorrow: You've hit today's limit for building with t.ROY. You can try again after {time} tomorrow. Your answers stay in this browser until then, unless you clear this computer.

tooBig.title: That was too much to send at once
tooBig.body: Your answers are too long to send in one piece. Go back, shorten the longest one, and try again.

timeout.title: t.ROY took too long
timeout.body: It didn't finish this time. Your answers are still here. Try again in a minute.

network.title: Couldn't reach t.ROY
network.body: Check that you're online, then try again. Your answers are still here.

other.title: Something went wrong on our end
other.body: t.ROY couldn't finish building this time. It wasn't anything you did. Your answers are still here. Try again.

live.working: Working on it. This usually takes about a minute.
live.long: This is taking longer than usual. It's still working, so stay on this page.

tour.checkedHere: Checked right here in your browser.
tour.done: That's what I see on this page. Tap a note to find its line.
tour.readNote: I read it top to bottom. Nothing big jumped out. Your new page is coming.

blank.first: There's a blank still sitting on this line. The new page won't print blanks, and I check for them before it's called done.
blank.again: Another blank here. Same fix: it comes off or gets your real detail.

emptySection.first: This part says there's nothing in it. The new page just leaves a section off when there's nothing for it.
emptySection.again: Same here. An empty section comes off.

missingTitle.first: This job is missing a title or a company name. Employers look for both. If one is still missing on the new page, I'll flag it so you can fill it in.
missingTitle.again: This one is missing a title or a company too. I'll flag it the same way.

noDates.first: This job has no dates on it. Employers notice that fast. The new page won't guess a date, and if one is missing I'll flag it for you to fill in.
noDates.again: No dates on this job either. Same deal: no guessing, and I'll flag it.

datelessPage.first: There are no dates anywhere on this page. That reads like something is being hidden. The new page goes by date, using only the dates you give.
datelessPage.again: Still no dates here. The new page goes by date.

toolMark.first: This line names a resume tool. The new page reads as yours, with no tool's name on it.
toolMark.again: Another tool name here. It comes off.

dash.first: Long dashes like this one can make a page read as machine-made. The new page uses plain periods and commas.
dash.again: Another long dash. Same fix on the new page.

dashRange.first: That long dash in the dates can read as machine-made. The new page uses a plain hyphen.
dashRange.again: Same long dash in these dates. Plain hyphen on the new page.

soleActor.first: Another line on this page says you helped with this work. This line makes it sound like you did it alone. The new page keeps shared work shared.
soleActor.again: Same here: shared work stays shared on the new page.

credentialStatus.first: This one has no year or status on it, so a reader can't tell if it's still good. The new page won't guess, so have that answer ready.
credentialStatus.again: Same with this one: no year or status. Have it ready.

generic.first: This line is worth a second look. The new page gets checked line by line against your own words.
generic.again: This one too. It gets the same line-by-line check.

quality.objective: An objective tells the employer what you want. They're reading to see what you bring, so this spot gets a few true lines about your work instead.
quality.summary: There's no summary up top. Two or three true lines about what you do and what you bring tell a reader why to keep going.
quality.genericSummary: This line could sit on anybody's page, so it tells a reader nothing about you. A summary works when it carries facts only you have.
quality.softSkillList: Anybody can type these words, so a reader skips right past them. Skills are things you could be tested on, like tools and machines; your bullets show the rest.
quality.weakBullet: This names a task but not what you did with it. A bullet starts with the action, so a reader sees the work.
quality.gerund: This starts with an -ing word, so it reads like a list of chores. A bullet starts with the action itself, like Trained instead of Training.
quality.vague: This could sit under any job, so it tells a reader nothing. A bullet names one real thing you did.
quality.bullets: This is a block of words, not bullets. A hiring manager skims, so each thing you did gets its own bullet that starts with the action.
quality.bare: These are bare words under a job, not bullets. A reader can't tell what you did with them.
quality.headingMissing: Your jobs sit here with no heading over them. A reader and the hiring software look for a plain heading like EXPERIENCE to find them.
quality.headingOdd: A reader and the hiring software don't know this heading. Plain ones like EXPERIENCE, SKILLS and EDUCATION get found fast.
quality.headingMixed: This heading looks different from your others. Matching headings read as careful, and mixed ones read as rushed.
quality.did: "Did" is a weak start. Lead with the action itself so a reader sees the work.
quality.dutyLabel: A duties label turns what's under it into a job description. A reader wants what you did, one bullet at a time.
quality.dutyPosting: "{phrase}" reads like the job posting. The employer already knows what the job was; this line should say what you did in it.

qualityAgain.dutyPhrasing: Same thing here: this says what the job was, not what you did.
qualityAgain.weakBullet: Same here: this line needs a real action.
qualityAgain.bullets: Same here: words under a job, not bullets.
qualityAgain.genericSummary: This one could sit on anybody's page too.
qualityAgain.heading: Same with this heading.
qualityAgain.default: Same kind of weak spot on this line.
